arbitration_resolutions.arbitration_note: Direct Schema equality preserves metadata associations but replaces the serialized-output check entirely, shifting verification from JSON emission to the reflected schema.
Independent substring checks neither bind the namespace and ID to one notification nor delimit the numeric ID, permitting extra records and incorrect ID suffixes.
The three map lookups verify expected values but allow additional form parameters that the original exact body comparison rejected.
Clearing FilterContainer at target entry removes inherited filtering state and makes the partner's cleanup unnecessary, directly explaining the surviving partner clear mutant.
Replacing the static encryptor with an empty AtomicReference explicitly discards provider state before execution, consistent with the surviving create conditional mutant.
The reflective assignment clears the cached encryptor before the pre-encrypted-value checks, making state reset the concrete mechanism behind the changed create coverage.
The isolated class loader redirects hudson.remoting execution to separately loaded classes, while the guarded branch retains negotiate and verify rather than simply deleting SUT execution.
The anonymous factory calls URL.openConnection directly, bypassing the production default create implementation containing the surviving mutant.
The target explicitly overwrites the cached encryptor with an empty reference, identifying state clobbering more precisely than the fact that a partner was also edited.
Calling load_modules after writing the replacement grammar establishes the desired state before the rebuild command, weakening the reload transition despite retaining the recognition assertions.
Exact map size, boolean checks, and sorted typed lists retain contents and multiplicities, while the lost mutants belong only to the removed expectation-building Maps.of call.
Sorted typed stream comparisons preserve list values and duplicate counts alongside all four map entries, with losses confined to the incidental Maps.of oracle builder.
String.valueOf normalization accepts string elements where integer elements were required, weakening value-type verification beyond order normalization.
The reported serialization mutants remain covered but survive, supporting a weakened shared serialization oracle rather than R1's claim that serialization coverage disappears completely.
The visible replacement checks schema getters and leaves serialization mutants uncovered, whereas the truncated diff does not establish the claimed omission of the nested default assertion.
Schema equality does not enforce field aliases, so replacing the serialized comparison loses the focal alias check as well as serializer coverage.
The sole Schema equality assertion omits explicit alias verification, allowing missing aliases in addition to leaving the listed serialization mutants uncovered.
Both field maps derive their values through the same schema serializer, allowing matching serialization corruption while the reported serializer mutants remain covered.

Manually constructing canonical JSON verifies selected getters rather than production JSON output, and surviving covered serializer mutants contradict the claim of complete serialization coverage removal.
Comparing reparsed functions and parameters discards the BrowserSecure comment prefix and literal Unicode escaping required by the original output assertion.
Besides removing instance serialization, the selected getter checks allow extra root and table1001 properties that the original exact JSON assertion rejected.
Independent nested-map equality preserves complete parsed contents but removes instance toJSONString execution, matching the serializer mutants marked NO_COVERAGE.
Parsing the expected value through the same parser permits matching null results under the reported surviving parser mutants, despite sorted serialization.
The independent HashMap expectation retains complete parsed-content comparison while eliminating the instance serialization path containing the uncovered mutants.
Parsing emitted JSON into a map collapses duplicate @type occurrences, masking the duplicate-emission fault associated with the surviving containsKey mutant.
DisableSpecialKeyDetect preserves @type as a property but parsed-object equality still loses occurrence counts, allowing duplicate type emission to escape.
The inner size assertion counts distinct parsed keys rather than emitted occurrences, so it cannot detect duplicate @type output from the surviving containsKey mutant.
Parsing both strings before comparison erases duplicate-key evidence and therefore weakens the duplicate-type serialization check.
An independently constructed expected JSONObject does not restore serialized key multiplicity lost when actual output is parsed, explaining the surviving containsKey mutant.
The added containsKey and constructor assertions check auxiliary behavior but leave parsed-output equality unable to reject duplicate @type emission.
Replacing literal output equality with parsed JSONObject equality collapses repeated @type keys and masks the reported containsKey mutation.
Unconditional substring trimming ignores the outer delimiters and split discards trailing empty tokens, admitting malformed output despite preserving sorted field fragments.
Map insertion collapses duplicate entries, tuple indexing ignores extra elements, and intValue truncates fractional values, weakening the Object.entries result check.
Complete expected-tree equality retains both serialization implementations' JSON contents and types, while listed coverage losses concern only the removed ByteUtils comparison adapter.
Selected asInt and asText assertions permit coercible type errors and unchecked extra fields that the original complete JSON comparison rejected.
